title: Adentris vs Binario Research: AI Chart Audit Compared
summary: Adentris vs Binario Research for behavioral health and SUD: daily accreditation-ready chart audits versus real-time, pre-submission revenue integrity with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and denials.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Adentris and Binario Research both use AI to audit behavioral health documentation, and they are close on the core idea: check charts against requirements instead of sampling by hand. The differences that matter are focus and timing. Binario Research is known for daily AI chart audits that keep programs ready for accreditation and payer inspections, mapping your own standards and payer rules into continuous checks. Adentris reviews notes in real time before the claim is submitted, is built around SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2, drafts the correction in the moment, and pairs review with an appeals and denials module. If your priority is accreditation-ready QA, Binario fits. If it is denials and pre-submission revenue integrity, that is where Adentris focuses.


Both audit behavioral health charts, so the comparison comes down to what the audit is for and when it happens. Here is the honest breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What Binario Research does


Binario Research is an AI-powered chart audit and quality-assurance layer that works on top of your EMR for behavioral health, SUD, detox, residential, PHP, IOP, and outpatient programs. It performs daily chart audits, flags documentation gaps, sends alerts to clinicians, and maps your documentation standards, program rules, and payer requirements into continuous checks, with an emphasis on staying ready for JCAHO, CARF, and state inspections. It supports HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 oversight. For multi-location programs whose priority is continuous, accreditation-ready quality assurance, Binario is a strong option.

## Which should you choose?


Both audit behavioral health charts against rules, so the real question is emphasis and timing. Binario Research is built around continuous, accreditation-ready QA: daily audits that map your standards and payer rules and alert the team to gaps. Adentris is built around catching the specific gaps that get behavioral health and SUD claims denied and fixing them before submission, in real time, with the correction drafted while the note is open and an appeals workflow when a payer pushes back. Both understand 42 CFR Part 2; Adentris adds ASAM level-of-care depth and pre-submission, claim-level timing, and it runs on any EHR through a secure web agent. A program can run Binario for accreditation QA and Adentris for revenue integrity.


- **Choose Binario Research if** your priority is continuous, accreditation-ready quality assurance with daily chart audits and gap alerts across your programs.
- **Choose Adentris if** you run a SUD or behavioral health program and the pain is denied claims: you want denial-driving gaps like ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2 caught and corrected before submission, with a paired appeals and denials module, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a Binario Research alternative for SUD revenue integrity


If your program uses Binario Research, or is evaluating it, the question is usually whether you want continuous auditing that flags gaps for the team to work or a layer that catches and corrects the gaps before the claim goes out, with SUD-specific rules built in. Many substance use disorder programs want the latter, because the claims they lose turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent, and they want the fix drafted in the moment rather than surfaced in a daily report. Adentris is built around exactly that, runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, and pairs review with an appeals and denials workflow, which makes it a natural revenue-integrity complement or alternative alongside accreditation-focused auditing.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. At Sobrius Health, a multi-site Virginia SUD provider, pre-submission documentation accuracy moved from 73% to 96%. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. ## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and Binario Research?**


Both are AI chart-audit platforms for behavioral health. Binario Research runs daily audits that map your standards and payer rules and keep you ready for accreditation and inspections. Adentris reviews notes in real time before the claim is submitted, drafts the correction, and is built around SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2, with a paired appeals and denials module, running on any EHR through a secure web agent. The main differences are focus (accreditation QA versus claim denials) and timing (daily audit versus pre-submission fix).


**Can Adentris and Binario Research be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use Binario Research to run daily accreditation-ready audits and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside Binario Research.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to Binario Research?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than accreditation-ready quality assurance, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. Binario Research is strong for continuous, accreditation-ready chart auditing across behavioral health and SUD. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
